questions.question_text: The radius of a hemisphere is doubled. How many times as large is the new volume?

options.why: Squared the scale factor ($2^{2}$) instead of cubing it.
Used the scale factor directly, without cubing it.

questions.solution_text:
$V = \frac{2}{3}\pi r^{3}$
Doubling the radius replaces $r$ with $2r$.
$V_{\text{new}} = \frac{2}{3}\pi (2r)^{3} = 8 \times \frac{2}{3}\pi r^{3}$
The new volume is $8$ times the original.

questions.question_text: A hemispherical bowl has a radius of $3$ cm. Zoe calculated its volume as $\frac{4}{3}\pi \times 3^{3}$ cm³. What is the correct volume, in cm³, correct to $2$ decimal places?

options.why: Used the whole-sphere formula instead of halving it for a hemisphere.
Squared the radius instead of cubing it ($r^{2}$ not $r^{3}$).

questions.solution_text:
A hemisphere is half a sphere, so halve the sphere volume.
$V = \frac{1}{2} \times \frac{4}{3}\pi r^{3}$
$= \frac{1}{2} \times \frac{4}{3} \times \pi \times 3^{3}$
$= 56.5486\ldots$
$\approx 56.55\text{ cm}^{3}$
